title: Repair & harden private control-plane auth path after upgrade-triggered token rejections
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: During a rolling upgrade of the private control plane (private-2026.02), a subset of agents began receiving 401/403 errors from the new auth proxy layer leading to degraded API connectivity for 18 customer VPCs over a 42-minute window. This ticket tracks the corrective action items, ownership, and roll-forward mitigations to both restore service and prevent recurrence.
impact_summary: 18 private deployments experienced intermittent control-plane API failures (agent heartbeats and key rotation calls) resulting in failed reconciles, increased reconnect attempts, and a spike in customer-visible API errors. No customer data was exfiltrated. Estimated customer-facing downtime window: 00:42 (start-to-stable). 12 customers reported transient errors during the window.
timeline_summary: 2026-02-28 03:10 UTC: rolling upgrade begins. 03:16 UTC: first 401 observed from agent heartbeats. 03:18-03:40 UTC: escalation and mitigation; rollback attempted for one batch. 03:52 UTC: global config change (auth proxy throttle backoff tweak) deployed and stabilized. 04:00 UTC: monitoring shows reduced 401s. 04:52 UTC: post-incident triage started.
root_cause: A config drift in the new auth proxy's token cache invalidation TTL combined with a previously undocumented client behavior (concurrent token refresh and replay on network flaps) resulted in short-lived token rejections. The upgraded auth proxy tightened validation and rejected near-expired tokens when replayed in a narrow timing window. This timing window was exacerbated by a temporary increase in control-plane latency during the upgrade batch.
immediate_mitigation: 1) Scoped rollback of the auth proxy config change for batches still pending. 2) Temporarily increased token acceptance window to accept tokens within 30s of expiry while we validated client refresh behavior. 3) Added circuit-breaker to reduce retry storms from agents. These steps restored control-plane connectivity within 42 minutes.
long_term_plan: 1) Add a conformance test for token race conditions and replay under simulated network flaps. 2) Enforce upgraded pre-upgrade canary that runs auth proxy upgrade against a synthetic agent workload to validate refresh/replay windows. 3) Publish a compatibility contract for token refresh semantics and integrate it into the private upgrade checklist. 4) Implement a safer progressive rollout with smaller batch sizes and automated rollback triggers tied to auth error rates.

notes: Engineering decision: we prioritized fast rollback and conservative acceptance window to restore availability; trade-off is a small time-based edge where near-expiry tokens could be accepted for 30s. Security has been looped in for sign-off.
Design consideration: UX surface for private customers will include an upgrade compatibility note in console and an explicit canary opt-in for risky upgrades.
Follow-up: run a tabletop in next incident retro to validate playbook clarity and cross-team ownership during upgrades. Invite Infra, Security, Platform, and SRE.
